items.title: Collocations for Giving and Receiving Criticism
items.description: Learn high-value word pairs (constructive feedback, take offense, broad criticism) for discussing feedback professionally.

items.title: Precise Synonyms for 'Increase' and 'Decrease'
items.description: Replace overused words with nuanced alternatives (surge, plummet, stabilize, fluctuate) to show advanced vocabulary range.

items.title: Essential Business and Economics Vocabulary
items.description: Master domain-specific terms (revenue stream, stakeholder, implement strategy, feasibility study) for task 1 reports and task 2 essays.

items.title: Emotions and Attitudes: Precise Word Choices
items.description: Go beyond 'happy' and 'sad' with words like 'resigned', 'apprehensive', 'ambivalent' to express complex feelings in essays.

items.title: Collocations and Phrases: Environment and Sustainability
items.description: Learn authentic phrases (carbon footprint, renewable energy, ecosystem degradation) commonly used in environmental discussion topics.

items.title: Hedging Language and Qualifiers
items.description: Use words and phrases (arguably, to some extent, relatively, fairly) to soften claims and show nuanced, critical thinking.

items.title: Verbs for Describing Research, Studies, and Findings
items.description: Master reporting verbs (correlate with, suggest that, indicate, propose) and their correct grammar for academic discussions.

items.title: Technology and Digital Vocabulary in Modern Context
items.description: Learn both mainstream and sophisticated terms (algorithm, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data breach) from contemporary domains.

items.title: Language of Persuasion and Argumentation
items.description: Use persuasive markers (undeniably, the evidence clearly shows, compelling reason) to strengthen task 2 essay arguments.

items.title: Word Families: Maximizing Vocabulary Range
items.description: Understand derivations and word families (act, active, activity, activate, action) to vary vocabulary sophistication throughout essays.

items.title: Formality Registers: Matching Tone to Task and Audience
items.description: Understand when to use formal (subsequently, facilitate), neutral, and slightly informal expressions for different IELTS task types.

items.title: Advanced Phrasal Verbs for Writing and Speaking
items.description: Use sophisticated phrasal verbs (bring about, set forth, account for, bear on) rather than single words to sound more natural and fluent.
